description: Queries where contexts contain conflicting information - system should mark as DISPUTED

cases.query: Did the project launch successfully?
contexts: The project launch was a complete success. All systems performed as expected and user adoption exceeded targets by 40%.
The project launch failed catastrophically. Critical bugs caused system outages affecting thousands of users.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: success vs failure
cases.rationale: One source says success, another says failure - cannot both be true

cases.query: Is the company profitable?
contexts: The company reported record profits of $2.3 billion in 2024, marking its fifth consecutive year of growth.
The company posted a net loss of $450 million in 2024, forcing layoffs of 15% of its workforce.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: profitable vs loss-making
cases.rationale: One source reports profits, another reports losses for the same period

cases.query: Was the medication approved by the FDA?
contexts: The FDA granted full approval for the medication in March 2024, citing strong efficacy data.
The FDA rejected the medication's application in March 2024 due to insufficient safety data.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: approved vs rejected
cases.rationale: One source says approved, another says rejected - mutually exclusive

cases.query: Did sales increase this quarter?
contexts: Sales increased 25% quarter-over-quarter, driven by strong demand in the Asian market.
Sales declined 18% compared to last quarter as supply chain issues impacted availability.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: increase vs decrease
cases.rationale: One source reports increase, another reports decrease

cases.query: Is the CEO stepping down?
contexts: The CEO announced his resignation effective immediately, citing personal reasons.
The CEO confirmed he will remain in his role for at least another three years.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: leaving vs staying
cases.rationale: One source says resigning, another says staying

cases.query: Did the defendant plead guilty?
contexts: The defendant entered a guilty plea to all charges in court this morning.
The defendant pleaded not guilty and requested a jury trial.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: guilty vs not guilty plea
cases.rationale: One source says guilty plea, another says not guilty

cases.query: Was the concert cancelled?
contexts: The concert was cancelled due to severe weather conditions. All ticket holders will receive refunds.
The concert went ahead as scheduled despite weather concerns. Over 50,000 fans attended.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: cancelled vs proceeded
cases.rationale: One source says cancelled, another says it proceeded

cases.query: Did the bill pass in Congress?
contexts: The bill passed the House with a vote of 245-190 and now heads to the Senate.
The bill failed to pass the House, falling 15 votes short of the required majority.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: passed vs failed
cases.rationale: One source says passed, another says failed

cases.query: Is the product available for pre-order?
contexts: Pre-orders are now open on the official website with shipping expected in December.
The company confirmed that pre-orders have been delayed indefinitely due to supply issues.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: available vs delayed
cases.rationale: One source says pre-orders open, another says delayed indefinitely

cases.query: Did the team win the championship?
contexts: The team won the championship with a dramatic last-second victory, their first title in 20 years.
The team lost the championship game in overtime, extending their title drought to 21 years.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: won vs lost
cases.rationale: One source says won, another says lost

cases.query: How much did the stock price change today?
contexts: The stock surged 12% today following better-than-expected earnings.
The stock dropped 8% today as investors reacted to disappointing guidance.
cases.description: Direct numerical contradiction: up vs down
cases.rationale: One source says +12%, another says -8%

cases.query: Is the restaurant open on Sundays?
contexts: The restaurant is open seven days a week, including Sundays from 10am to 9pm.
The restaurant is closed on Sundays for staff rest days.
cases.description: Direct contradiction: open vs closed
cases.rationale: One source says open on Sundays, another says closed

cases.query: What is the effectiveness rate of the vaccine?
contexts: Clinical trials showed the vaccine was 95% effective at preventing symptomatic infection.
Real-world data found the vaccine was only 64% effective against the Delta variant.
A UK study reported 88% effectiveness against hospitalization.
cases.description: Numerical disagreement across different studies
cases.rationale: Different studies report 95%, 64%, and 88% - significant variation

cases.query: When was the Great Wall of China built?
contexts: The Great Wall was primarily built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644).
Construction began during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang around 221 BC.
Archaeological evidence suggests wall-building dates back to the 7th century BC.
cases.description: Different historical accounts giving different time periods
cases.rationale: Sources give Ming Dynasty, Qin Dynasty, and 7th century BC

cases.query: What caused the dinosaur extinction?
contexts: The asteroid impact theory, supported by the Chicxulub crater, is now the scientific consensus.
Volcanic activity from the Deccan Traps caused climate change that killed the dinosaurs.
It was a combination of asteroid impact and volcanic activity that led to extinction.
cases.description: Competing scientific theories for the same event
cases.rationale: Three different theories: asteroid, volcanic, or combination

cases.query: How many people died in the Titanic sinking?
contexts: The British inquiry concluded that 1,503 people died when the Titanic sank.
The US Senate investigation put the death toll at 1,517.
Recent analysis suggests the number may be closer to 1,496.
cases.description: Different authoritative sources give different numbers
cases.rationale: British says 1,503, US says 1,517, modern analysis says 1,496

cases.query: What is the company's market share?
contexts: According to Gartner, the company holds 32% of the global market.
IDC reports the company's market share at 24%.
Internal company reports claim 38% market share based on revenue.
cases.description: Different analyst firms report different market shares
cases.rationale: Gartner says 32%, IDC says 24%, company claims 38%

cases.query: When did the company go public?
contexts: The company completed its IPO on March 15, 2020, raising $2.5 billion.
The company's IPO took place on March 22, 2020, with shares priced at $68.
cases.description: Different dates for the same IPO event
cases.rationale: One source says March 15, another says March 22

cases.query: What is the population of the city?
contexts: The 2023 census recorded the city population at 2.4 million residents.
City planning estimates put the current population at approximately 2.8 million.
The United Nations demographic report lists the population as 2.1 million.
cases.description: Different official sources give different population figures
cases.rationale: Census says 2.4M, city estimates 2.8M, UN says 2.1M

cases.query: What causes migraines?
contexts: Migraines are caused by abnormal brain activity affecting nerve signals and blood vessels.
Research indicates migraines result from genetic mutations affecting ion channels.
The latest theory suggests migraines originate from dysfunction in the brainstem.
cases.description: Multiple competing medical theories
cases.rationale: Different theories: nerve signals, genetic mutations, brainstem dysfunction

cases.query: How many jobs will AI eliminate?
contexts: McKinsey estimates AI will eliminate 85 million jobs globally by 2030.
The World Economic Forum predicts AI will create 97 million new jobs by 2025.
Goldman Sachs research suggests 300 million jobs could be affected by AI automation.
cases.description: Wildly different predictions from major institutions
cases.rationale: McKinsey: 85M eliminated, WEF: 97M created, Goldman: 300M affected

cases.query: What is the average house price in the area?
contexts: Zillow reports the median home price in the area is $485,000.
Redfin data shows the median at $520,000 for the same region.
The local real estate board reports an average price of $450,000.
cases.description: Different real estate sources give different prices
cases.rationale: Zillow: $485K, Redfin: $520K, local board: $450K

cases.query: When was the painting created?
contexts: Art historians date the painting to 1503-1506 based on stylistic analysis.
Recent scientific analysis suggests the painting was completed around 1517.
Historical records indicate the artist began the work in 1495.
cases.description: Different dating methods yield different results
cases.rationale: Stylistic: 1503-1506, scientific: 1517, historical: 1495

cases.query: How much water should you drink daily?
contexts: The standard recommendation is 8 glasses (64 oz) of water per day.
The National Academy of Medicine recommends 125 oz daily for men and 91 oz for women.
Recent research suggests water needs vary widely and there is no one-size-fits-all amount.
cases.description: Conflicting health recommendations
cases.rationale: Traditional: 64oz, NAM: 91-125oz, research: varies

cases.query: What is the unemployment rate?
contexts: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports unemployment at 3.7%.
The broader U-6 measure, which includes underemployed workers, stands at 7.1%.
Independent economists argue the true rate is closer to 10% when including discouraged workers.
cases.description: Different measures give different unemployment figures
cases.rationale: BLS: 3.7%, U-6: 7.1%, independent: ~10%

cases.query: What is the best diet for weight loss?
contexts: Low-carb diets like keto show the fastest short-term weight loss in clinical trials.
Mediterranean diet studies show the best long-term weight maintenance and health outcomes.
Research indicates calorie restriction regardless of macros is the primary driver of weight loss.
cases.description: Different dietary approaches with conflicting evidence
cases.rationale: Keto: fastest short-term, Mediterranean: best long-term, calories: primary driver

cases.query: Is remote work more productive than office work?
contexts: A Stanford study found remote workers were 13% more productive, with fewer breaks.
Microsoft research showed that while individual productivity increased, collaboration suffered.
A Harvard study found productivity varied by role - creative work suffered while routine tasks improved.
Managers reported difficulty assessing remote productivity, suggesting measurement bias.
cases.description: Nuanced disagreement - depends on how productivity is measured
cases.rationale: Studies conflict: individual productivity up, but collaboration and creativity down

cases.query: Is coffee good for your health?
contexts: Research found coffee drinkers had 10-15% lower risk of death from heart disease.
Studies show coffee can increase anxiety, disrupt sleep, and raise blood pressure.
Health effects depend heavily on genetics, particularly the CYP1A2 gene.
Pregnant women are advised to limit coffee due to risks to fetal development.
cases.description: Context-dependent - benefits and risks both exist
cases.rationale: Good for heart, bad for sleep/anxiety, depends on genetics and pregnancy

cases.query: Does screen time harm children's development?
contexts: A major study found no significant link between screen time and psychological problems in teens.
Research shows excessive screen time correlates with increased anxiety and depression in children.
Longitudinal studies suggest the type of content matters more than total screen time.
Critics note most screen time research relies on self-reported data, which is unreliable.
cases.description: Conflicting research with methodological concerns
cases.rationale: Studies conflict, content matters, and methodology is questioned

cases.query: Are electric vehicles better for the environment?
contexts: Over their lifetime, EVs produce 50-70% less CO2 than gasoline cars even with current grid mix.
EV battery production creates significant environmental damage through mining rare earth metals.
The environmental benefit depends heavily on local electricity sources - coal vs renewable.
Battery recycling infrastructure is inadequate, creating future environmental liabilities.
cases.description: Complex tradeoffs - depends on factors like grid mix and mining
cases.rationale: Lower lifetime emissions but mining damage, grid-dependent, recycling issues

cases.query: What caused the Roman Empire to fall?
contexts: Historian Edward Gibbon argued that Christianity weakened Roman military virtue and civic duty.
Economic historians point to currency debasement and unsustainable military spending.
Climate researchers have linked the fall to a period of severe drought and crop failures.
Recent scholarship emphasizes the gradual transformation rather than sudden 'fall' narrative.
cases.description: Multiple competing historical theories
cases.rationale: Christianity, economics, climate, or gradual transformation - historians disagree

cases.query: Does the minimum wage increase cause unemployment?
contexts: Classical economic theory predicts minimum wage increases reduce employment.
The famous Card-Krueger study found no negative employment effects from minimum wage increases.
Recent studies using better methodology found small negative effects on hours worked.
Effects vary significantly by region, industry, and the size of the increase.
cases.description: Economic research with conflicting findings
cases.rationale: Theory says yes, Card-Krueger says no, newer studies find small effects

cases.query: Is social media harmful to mental health?
contexts: Studies link heavy social media use to increased rates of depression and anxiety in teens.
Research shows social media can provide community support and reduce isolation for many users.
The relationship is complex - passive consumption harms while active engagement benefits.
Critics note that correlation studies cannot establish causation in either direction.
cases.description: Depends on usage patterns - both harm and benefit documented
cases.rationale: Harmful for heavy use, beneficial for community, depends on active vs passive

cases.query: How many species are there on Earth?
contexts: Current scientific estimates suggest approximately 8.7 million species exist on Earth.
A 2023 study using AI analysis estimates up to 100 million species may exist.
Traditional taxonomy-based counts put the number at around 2 million described species.
Deep sea and microbial diversity suggests true numbers could be orders of magnitude higher.
cases.description: Estimates vary by orders of magnitude
cases.rationale: Estimates range from 2M described to 100M possible - huge uncertainty

cases.query: Does homework improve student achievement?
contexts: Meta-analyses show homework has positive effects on achievement, especially in high school.
Research finds no correlation between homework and test scores in elementary school.
The quality and type of homework matters more than quantity for learning outcomes.
International comparisons show countries with less homework often outperform high-homework nations.
cases.description: Conflicting evidence across age groups and countries
cases.rationale: Positive in high school, no effect in elementary, international data contradicts

cases.query: What causes autism?
contexts: Research strongly supports a genetic basis, with hundreds of genes implicated.
Environmental factors during pregnancy, including infections, may play a role.
Some scientists propose the rise in autism rates is primarily due to expanded diagnostic criteria.
The exact causes remain unknown, with most cases likely involving multiple factors.
cases.description: Multiple theories with no consensus on causation
cases.rationale: Genetic, environmental, diagnostic changes, or multifactorial - no consensus

cases.query: Is nuclear power safe?
contexts: Per unit of energy, nuclear has the lowest death rate of any power source including renewables.
Accidents like Chernobyl and Fukushima demonstrate catastrophic failure potential.
Modern reactor designs are passively safe and cannot melt down like older designs.
Long-term nuclear waste storage remains an unsolved problem spanning thousands of years.
cases.description: Safe by statistics but with catastrophic tail risks
cases.rationale: Lowest death rate but catastrophic accidents possible, waste unsolved

cases.query: How many galaxies are in the universe?
contexts: The Hubble Space Telescope observations estimated approximately 200 billion galaxies.
Newer analysis suggests the actual number may be closer to 2 trillion galaxies.
Recent James Webb data indicates even more galaxies in the early universe than expected.
The observable universe contains a finite number, but the total universe may be infinite.
cases.description: Estimates have changed dramatically with new observations
cases.rationale: Hubble: 200B, newer: 2T, JWST finding more - order of magnitude uncertainty

cases.query: What determines intelligence?
contexts: Twin studies suggest intelligence is 50-80% heritable, indicating strong genetic influence.
Environmental factors like education, nutrition, and socioeconomic status significantly impact IQ.
The Flynn effect shows IQ scores have risen dramatically over generations despite stable genetics.
Many researchers argue IQ tests measure only narrow cognitive abilities, not true intelligence.
cases.description: Nature vs nurture debate with no clear resolution
cases.rationale: Genetics 50-80%, but environment matters, IQ rising, tests may be flawed

cases.query: Is organic food healthier?
contexts: A Stanford meta-analysis found no significant nutritional differences between organic and conventional.
Studies show organic produce has lower pesticide residues, which may benefit health long-term.
Organic farming practices are better for soil health and biodiversity.
Some organic-approved pesticides are more toxic than synthetic alternatives they replace.
cases.description: No nutritional difference but other factors complicate the picture
cases.rationale: No nutritional benefit, but less pesticide, better environment, organic pesticides exist
